# Appeal of Denial — Request for Reconsideration

**Quinn Novak**
[Street address]
[City, State ZIP]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

**Date:** [Date this letter is sent]

**To:** [Appeals address printed on my denial notice]
Kansas Medicaid — [Name of my managed-care plan, if applicable]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-02**
- **Member:** Quinn Novak
- **Member ID:** W763701748
- **Reference number:** POC-7321626800-52420
- **Service denied:** Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
- **Reason given:** Records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment
- **Appeal deadline stated in the notice:** 2027-01-29

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

**A note on the governing policy at the outset:** the denial notice tells me the decision was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria, but it does not name that policy or send me a copy of it, and no policy language has been provided to me. For that reason, I am not quoting the plan anywhere in this letter — I have no plan text in front of me to quote. Everything below is drawn from my own medical records. I ask the plan to supply the criteria it actually applied, as I request in a separate paragraph below.

I am appealing the denial of coverage for a total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, orthopedic surgery. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery.

## The reason given for the denial

The notice states that my records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. My records show that I completed a substantial course of conservative treatment over more than a year before surgery was requested. I am setting out below exactly what those records contain.

## What my records document

**Length of symptoms.** I have had 14 months of progressive pain in the shoulder, and the pain is not relieved by rest.

**Supervised physical therapy.** I completed supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening, 16 weeks in length, from 2026-03-14 to 2026-07-04, with 18 visits completed. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note.

**Medication.** I took NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief. I also received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-09, which gave me 2 weeks of partial relief.

**Imaging.** Shoulder radiographs on 2026-05-27 (true AP and axillary) show complete loss of glenohumeral joint space with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis and a flattened glenoid. CT confirms an intact rotator cuff.

**Physical examination.** My exam shows glenohumeral crepitus, active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees and external rotation to 10 degrees, with cuff strength intact.

**Function.** I cannot reach overhead, dress without help, or sleep on the affected side.

**Surgical risk factors.** I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker.

My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, submitted this documentation with the prior authorization request and has documented that the procedure is needed.

## Why I am asking for reconsideration

The single reason given for the denial is the absence of an adequate conservative-treatment trial. My chart documents 16 weeks and 18 visits of supervised physical therapy, 4 months of NSAIDs, and a corticosteroid injection, all before surgery was requested, across 14 months of symptoms that have continued to progress. Each of those measures was tried and each fell short: the NSAIDs gave inadequate relief and the injection gave 2 weeks of partial relief. Meanwhile the imaging shows complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space, and my movement is limited to 90 degrees of forward elevation and 10 degrees of external rotation.

Because the plan has not told me what it counts as an adequate trial — no duration, number of visits, or other threshold has been stated to me in writing — I cannot show point by point that my care meets a specific standard. I can only show what my records contain, which is what I have done above. If the plan applied a specific requirement that my documented care did not meet, I ask that the requirement be identified and that I be told which part of my treatment history fell short of it.

## Request for the criteria the plan applied

The plan holds the clinical criteria used to decide my request, and I am asking for them in writing. Please send me **the clinical criteria applied to my prior authorization**, including the specific conservative-treatment requirement relied on in this denial, and please identify the medical policy referenced in the notice. I am copying the Kansas Medicaid agency on this request. If those criteria were applied by a review vendor rather than by the plan directly, please identify the vendor and provide the criteria it used.

## What I am asking for

I ask that the plan overturn the denial of CPT 23472 and authorize the total shoulder replacement. If the plan upholds the denial, I ask for a written explanation that identifies the specific criterion I did not meet and points to the part of my record the reviewer relied on, along with the name and specialty of the reviewing clinician. I also ask to be told how to request a state fair hearing.

I understand from the notice that my appeal must be received by 2027-01-29, and I am submitting it well ahead of that date. I am sending this to the appeal address printed on my denial notice. I understand I may also appeal through my managed-care plan or the Kansas Medicaid agency, and that I may request a state fair hearing; if any part of this appeal has been sent to the wrong place, please forward it to the correct office and let me know at the phone number above. I can also be reached through the member line on the back of my insurance card.

Thank you for taking another look at my case.

Sincerely,

**Quinn Novak**
Member ID: W763701748
[Signature]
[Date signed]

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-02 (reference POC-7321626800-52420)
- Physical therapy discharge note, 2026-03-14 to 2026-07-04
- Shoulder radiograph and CT reports, 2026-05-27
- Office notes from Dr. Lindqvist, orthopedic surgery
- [Any additional records I am including]

**cc:** Kansas Medicaid agency — [address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

evidence.submission_route: Medicaid is run by your state. Appeal through your state Medicaid agency or your managed-care plan, and you can also ask for a state fair hearing. All of the details are on your denial letter. By phone: the number on the back of your insurance card Deadline: Often just 30 to 90 days — act quickly and check your letter -- but your denial letter is authoritative. Use the appeal address printed on your denial letter.
evidence.criteria_request: Most state Medicaid programs publish the rules for HOW a decision must be made but not the medical criteria for a specific surgery - those usually sit with your managed-care plan or its review vendor. Ask your plan in writing for 'the clinical criteria applied to my prior authorization', and copy your state Medicaid agency. Massachusetts, North Carolina and California are the exceptions - they publish real procedure criteria.
